data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If the token budget accounting is itself recorded as an event in the same append-only log, budget exhaustion creates a circular dependency that can corrupt the append-only identity: the event recording 'budget exhausted' must itself be written, consuming tokens. If exhaustion occurs during the write of this accounting event, the chain is torn at the very moment the system is trying to record why it is halting. Resumption must be refused whenever budget state and event log are coupled in the same append-only structure, unless the budget-exhaustion record is written via a separate out-of-band channel. This is a counterexample to the claim that pure event sourcing alone guarantees resumability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The budget-exhausted event is written to a separate out-of-band log, not the main event chain, so the main chain's integrity is independent of budget accounting.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The system reserves budget for the halt-marker event before beginning any other event generation, guaranteeing the halt marker can always be written.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The budget accountant operates at a layer below the event log (e.g., the harness controls budget, not the event-sourced application), so the application never needs to write a budget event.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The halt marker is optional\u2014its absence does not indicate corruption, only that the halt was due to external budget enforcement rather than internal accounting.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The system uses a two-phase commit for the halt marker: prepare (budget-free metadata write) then commit, and exhaustion can only prevent the commit phase, leaving a recoverable prepared marker.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a naive event-sourced system, every state change\u2014including budget updates\u2014is an event. When budget is exhausted, the system must write a 'budget_exhausted' event, but writing that event requires budget it no longer has. If it writes it anyway (accounting debt), the event may partially commit, breaking the chain. If it does not write it, the log lacks a halt marker, and resumption cannot distinguish a clean halt from a crash. The coupling between budget state and event log creates an inherent partial-write risk at the exhaustion boundary. Decoupling budget accounting from the event log (external ledger) is necessary for clean halts.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
